title: Implement historical replay clock and as-of deterministic event provider
description:
Build the base of the production historical replay/backtest subsystem: a simulated Clock and an as-of historical MarketDataProvider. Later phase-q tasks (execution simulator, runner/manifest, CLI, integrity tests) build on these. This is production code, not a disposable script.

1. mike_trade/backtest/clock.py: implement ReplayClock. It conforms to the application's existing Clock port, so engine/scheduler/strategy code reads time only through it.
   - Time is timezone-aware UTC. It only moves forward, through explicit advance_to(t) calls driven by the replay event loop. Trying to move backwards or pass a naive datetime raises an error.
   - It must not read the wall clock or sleep in real time.
   - It exposes America/New_York session presentation through the existing exchange session calendar in mike_trade/scheduling/calendar.py. Covered: regular open/close, early closes, holidays/no-session days, session boundaries.

2. mike_trade/backtest/feed.py: implement HistoricalReplayFeed, a MarketDataProvider adapter. It is injected in place of the live Alpaca feed and wraps a bounded, operator-supplied, offline dataset: in-memory records or local fixture files. No network download.
   - It carries explicit provenance through a DataProvenance value: source, feed (for example IEX, not consolidated SIP), revision/vintage, adjustment policy and dataset content hash.
   - It emits events in strict chronological order with a deterministic tie-break for equal timestamps: event kind, then symbol, then sequence.
   - Point-in-time availability: a 1-minute bar covering [t, t+1m) becomes available only at its completion time t+1m plus an optional configured availability latency. Developing/partial candles are never exposed as completed. as_of(t) queries never return any record with availability time > t.
   - Future-adjusted data is refused (fail closed) unless the provenance declares it point-in-time. This includes split-adjusted series that use adjustment factors announced after the evaluation time, and revised bars whose revision vintage is later than the evaluation time.
   - Splits are represented as dated corporate-action events that are applied only from their effective time.
   - Halts, gaps and missing bars are surfaced as explicit data-quality markers that reuse the existing freshness/quality types. They are never forward-filled into synthetic bars.
   - Quotes/bid-ask: if the dataset has no quotes, the feed reports quote fidelity as UNAVAILABLE. When quotes exist but are sampled, it reports them as BAR_DERIVED/SAMPLED. Downstream fill logic can then flag the limitation instead of assuming quote evidence.
   - A deterministic seed is accepted and exposed for any randomized tie-breaking or jitter. The same dataset + seed must yield an identical event sequence.
   - All prices/volumes/quantities are Decimal.

3. tests/unit/test_replay_clock.py: positive and negative tests for both modules, using only small synthetic in-memory fixtures. No network, no credentials, no Alpaca client imports.

Before editing, inspect:
- mike_trade/market_data/ports.py (MarketDataProvider port and bar/quote types)
- mike_trade/domain/market.py (bar, quote and provenance value types)
- mike_trade/market_data/candles.py and mike_trade/market_data/context.py (completed-bar semantics, session VWAP context)
- mike_trade/market_data/quality.py (freshness/gap/halt markers)
- mike_trade/scheduling/calendar.py (exchange session calendar, early closes)
- the existing Clock port and any system/fake clock implementations under mike_trade/
- mike_trade/shadow/scenarios.py (how a feed is fanned out to consumers)

Decision budget: if an existing port shape is ambiguous, adapt to it with a thin adapter class in feed.py or clock.py rather than changing the port. Record the choice in a module docstring.
acceptance_criteria: mike_trade/backtest/clock.py defines ReplayClock satisfying the existing Clock port; its now() always returns a tz-aware UTC datetime
ReplayClock.advance_to raises on a backwards move or a naive datetime, and the module never calls datetime.now, time.time or time.sleep
ReplayClock reports session state (pre-open, regular, closed, early close) via the existing session calendar for a fixture that includes a holiday and an early-close day
mike_trade/backtest/feed.py defines HistoricalReplayFeed and DataProvenance; provenance includes source, feed, revision/vintage, adjustment policy and dataset content hash
A 1-minute bar for [09:30, 09:31) ET is not returned by as_of(09:30:59 ET) and is returned by as_of(09:31:00 ET) when latency is zero; a test asserts both
as_of(t) never returns any record whose availability time is greater than t; a test asserts this over every event of a multi-symbol fixture
Events with identical timestamps are ordered by the documented deterministic tie-break, and two iterations with the same dataset and seed yield identical sequences
A dataset marked future-adjusted, or containing a revision vintage later than the evaluation time, is rejected fail-closed with an explicit error
A split event affects prices/quantities only from its effective time; bars before it are unchanged in as_of results
Missing bars, gaps and halts produce explicit quality markers, and no synthetic forward-filled bar is emitted
Quote fidelity is reported as UNAVAILABLE for a bars-only dataset
All price/volume values in emitted records are Decimal
Neither module imports an Alpaca client, an HTTP library or broker credential configuration
tests/unit/test_replay_clock.py exists with positive and negative tests and passes when run alone
forbidden_changes: modify files outside allowed_write_paths, including existing market_data ports, scheduling calendar or domain types
change PLAN_SKELETON.json or other planning artifacts
download or fetch historical data over the network, or read broker credentials
expose developing/partial candles as completed bars or forward-fill missing bars
read the wall clock or sleep in real time inside replay code
use float for prices, volumes or quantities
create live broker orders or run broad test suites/backtests
